statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk stays in the low band with no live Nasdaq-100 price path available inside the final hour of the weekend futures halt, while stress-side conditions remain high on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption, elevated crude, rising global long-end yields and a sharply weaker August consumer-sentiment read.

headline: Nasdaq-100 futures still halted with about half an hour to the scheduled CME restart; tail low, stress high on unresolved Hormuz disruption, a steepening long end and a weak consumer read
body:
No live Nasdaq-100 price path exists at this timestamp. CME equity index futures remain inside the weekend halt and are scheduled to restart near 22:00 UTC, roughly half an hour after this assessment, so the evaluation rests on the last completed cash session, verified cross-asset levels and the current macro and geopolitical backdrop rather than on observed intraday structure. Re-verification at this hour found the evidence set unchanged from the preceding assessment, with no new escalation reported.

The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 30,046.14, down 0.13% inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 30,762.20 52-week high, after a second consecutive winning week for the major U.S. indices. The September Nasdaq-100 futures contract last settled at 30,141.75, down 0.15%, and remains marked closed as of August 14. VIX finished at 14.25, down 2.60%, which keeps implied volatility subdued against the high stress reading. Treasury constant-maturity yields stood at 4.15% for the 2Y, 4.32% for the 5Y, 4.63% for the 10Y and 5.21% for the 30Y at the August 13 H.15 publication, with a 20-year sale due Wednesday into a steepening curve.

Friday's internals were split rather than one-way. Broadcom fell 5.94% while AMD rose 6.5% and Micron added 2.3%, and sector context from the shared delayed cross-asset feed shows technology down 0.46% with software groups down more than 1% on the latest session and megacap direction mixed at two advancers against six decliners. That dispersion argues for uncertainty rather than persistent directional efficiency.

The macro backdrop softened materially into the weekend. The preliminary August University of Michigan sentiment index fell to 51.0 from 55.2, a decline of roughly 8% against a consensus near 54.5, with expectations down 8.7% to 50.6 and year-ahead inflation expectations rising to 4.3%. July retail sales fell by the most in over a year. Those readings sit alongside financial conditions reported at their easiest since 1996, a combination that raises uncertainty about the Fed path without establishing a directional price mechanism.

The energy and geopolitical backdrop remains the dominant stress channel. WTI trades at $82.40, up 1.42% on the day and more than 5% on the week, with Brent at $88.52, as Strait of Hormuz traffic stays depressed at between eight and fifteen daily transits against roughly 130 before the conflict. Iran's foreign minister continues talks with Oman on shipping routes while linking any reopening to conditions on Washington, and two ADNOC-owned tankers were struck by drones in the strait on August 13. The headline set is genuinely two-sided rather than one-directional.

Tail therefore stays in the low band. The observed evidence contains no persistent no-retracement structure, no failed-retracement extension and no index holding near an extreme, and none of that can be observed at all while the market is halted. Stress remains high because an unresolved supply disruption, elevated crude, rising global long yields and a deteriorating consumer read can still produce a large but recoverable drawdown. A narrow observation window is flagged around the scheduled Sunday restart, where thin liquidity and weekend headline risk concentrate.

The week ahead adds known checkpoints rather than observed risk: Empire State and NAHB on Monday, housing starts, building permits and industrial production on Tuesday, the 20-year auction and July FOMC minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed survey and Walmart on Thursday, and flash PMIs on Friday. These are scheduled catalysts, and under the fixed mapping they inform stress and confidence until an actual price path is available to score.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available and uniformly green with EA_ON. Tail moved narrowly between 12 and 17, stress climbed from the high-60s into the low 80s through the European and U.S. weekend hours before easing back toward 72, and confidence ranged from 66 to 80. The entire window sits inside the cash-market weekend and the CME futures halt, so that trajectory reflects an accumulating energy, rates and consumer backdrop rather than any observed Nasdaq-100 price structure.
outlookSummary: The scheduled CME restart in the next hour carries the highest conditional tail of the forecast at 18, reflecting thin liquidity and an unresolved Hormuz headline set rather than observed structure. Asian and European hours are expected to normalise toward 13-14 if the reopening print is orderly. A secondary rise to 17 is carried across the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC and the first hour after it, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first genuine tail evidence of the new week, easing back to 13 by the 20:00 UTC cash close. Every forecast hour stays below the 20 threshold, so the mapping remains EA_ON throughout, with stress peaking at 75 around the restart and the U.S. open and easing toward the high-60s overnight.
